title: FAK Cache Value — Roll-up & Ablation
description: Is fak's cache method paying off, and which feature earned it? The Grafana twin of the `fak cachevalue feed` Slack card: Track 1 WITNESSED KV-prefix reuse and the Track 2 OBSERVED/projected-$ P&L (split by owner, never blended), plus the offline `fak ablate` feature arms. Source: fak cachevalue metrics /metrics (scrape job fak_cachevalue; start with `fak cachevalue metrics --serve`).

panels.title: Is fak's cache method paying off?

options.content:
**One question:** is fak's cache work paying off, and which feature moved the needle? This dashboard is the live twin of `fak cachevalue feed` (the Slack card) plus the offline `fak ablate` arms — the SAME two-track fold, re-projected as metrics.

**The fence is load-bearing.** *Track 1* (`fak_cachevalue_latest_reuse_ratio`, sessions) is **WITNESSED** realized KV-prefix reuse. *Track 2* (every `_usd` / `saved_token_equiv` family) is an **OBSERVED / projected $** cost model over labelled provider cache reads — never a fak-witnessed dollar, never blended into Track 1. The `owner` label keeps provider vs fak dollars split so a provider-only corpus can never read as a fak win.

Source: `fak cachevalue metrics --serve` (scrape job `fak_cachevalue`). Panels read `No data` until the `docs/nightrun/*.jsonl` ledgers exist — run `fak cachevalue feed --once` (or the nightrun) to populate them.

panels.title: Scrape
panels.description: Prometheus scrape health for the `fak_cachevalue` job. Start it with `fak cachevalue metrics --serve --addr 127.0.0.1:9097`.

panels.title: Verdict
panels.description: MEASURED once the two-track fold has enough rows; INSUFFICIENT otherwise. `report_present` (not shown) stays 1 whenever the exporter is alive, so a dead scrape reads as DOWN, not zero.

panels.title: Cumulative NET $
panels.description: OBSERVED/projected: running net $ through the latest period (rebate + shed − write premium − spend). The P&L headline; a cost projection, never a fak-witnessed dollar.

panels.title: Broke even?
panels.description: 1 once the cumulative net $ has crossed zero.

panels.title: API cost reduction
panels.description: OBSERVED/projected: percent cheaper than the uncached/uncompacted counterfactual.

panels.title: fak share of $
panels.description: Percent of avoided $ attributable to fak-authored cache work; the rest is provider prompt-cache. Absent until any $ is avoided.

panels.title: Latest reuse ratio
panels.description: WITNESSED: most recent weekly bucket's realized KV-prefix reuse. NOT a vs-naive multiple (that family is excluded by the report's #1066 fence).

panels.title: Multi-turn sessions
panels.description: WITNESSED: sessions with >1 turn — the only ones that can realize prefix reuse.

panels.title: Total sessions
panels.description: WITNESSED: all sessions folded into Track 1.

panels.title: Dollar-blind rows
panels.description: Rows with saved token-equiv but no trusted price — excluded from every $ column (honest omission, not a zero).

panels.title: Realized reuse ratio over time
panels.description: The WITNESSED headline reuse ratio as it moves across scrapes.

panels.title: Track 2 — OBSERVED / projected $ (P&L, never blended into Track 1)
Net $ over time (OBSERVED/projected)
panels.description: Running and per-period net $. A cost projection over labelled provider cache reads — side by side with Track 1, never summed into it.

panels.title: Saved token-equiv by owner
panels.description: provider = OBSERVED prompt-cache; fak = WITNESSED kernel-authored; total = their sum. Split so a provider-only corpus cannot read as a fak win.

panels.title: API cost avoided by owner ($)
panels.description: OBSERVED/projected $ avoided, split by owner. provider = read rebate net of write premium; fak = compaction saving (WITNESSED shed, $ projected).

panels.title: Observed spend
panels.description: OBSERVED: actual API spend over the folded rows.

panels.title: Counterfactual
panels.description: OBSERVED/projected: uncached/uncompacted spend the reduction is measured against.

panels.title: Usage rows
panels.description: WITNESSED: gateway/guard usage rows in the fleet aggregate.

panels.title: Kernel decisions
panels.description: WITNESSED: cumulative kernel admission decisions.

panels.title: $ avoided per day by owner
panels.description: OBSERVED/projected daily run-rate over the savings-row span. PROVISIONAL under the honest-window floor — check the flag to the right.

panels.title: Savings span (days)
panels.description: Days of savings rows the run-rate is computed over.

panels.title: Run-rate
panels.description: PROVISIONAL when the span is under the honest floor — the 30/90-day extrapolation is not yet settled.

panels.title: Compaction shed (tok)
panels.description: WITNESSED: context tokens fak compaction shed — the only source of session extension.

panels.title: Context extension (tok)
panels.description: WITNESSED: tokens the session window was extended by. Provider cache reads never enlarge the window, so only shed counts.

panels.title: Feature ablation — which feature moved the needle
How to read the ablation arms

options.content: **Offline, deterministic, $0.** These arms come from `fak ablate` replaying the SAME frozen trace with one feature toggled per arm — so `speedup_ratio > 1` is that feature's WITNESSED win over the `baseline` arm (marked in the table below), not a live provider measurement. Arms are labelled by `(arm, workload)`; a workload is a trace's content hash, so arms from different traces never share a bar. Populate by dropping `fak ablate` report JSONs in `experiments/ablate/` (a sample report ships with the repo; non-ablate JSONs there are skipped with a note).

panels.title: Ablate report
panels.description: 1 when at least one `fak ablate` report was folded.

panels.title: Arms
panels.description: Total ablation arms across every folded report.

panels.title: Speedup vs baseline by arm
panels.description: WITNESSED replay: baseline mean / this arm's mean. >1 is faster than the baseline arm (which sits at exactly 1).

panels.title: Mean decide latency by arm (ns)
panels.description: WITNESSED replay: per-arm mean kernel decide latency. Lower is the win the speedup ratio expresses.

panels.title: vDSO fast-path hits by arm
panels.description: WITNESSED replay: vDSO (fast-path) hits per arm — the mechanism the speedup comes from when the vdso feature is on.

panels.title: Baseline arm (speedup reference)
panels.description: The arm each speedup ratio is measured against, per workload.
